subject: Renewal + expansion — pricing & volume step-ups (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme-health.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Renewal + expansion — pricing & volume step-ups (post-call recap)

Hi Jordan / Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Recap:
- Current contract: 6M tokens/month baseline, mostly routed to model-redwood-v1.
- Goal: 12–18M tokens/month within next 6–9 months, plus adding a new "evaluation" route for Gen2 model variants (~25–30% of traffic initially).
- Primary asks from Acme: predictable unit economics, target $/1M tokens for budgeting, and blended rate guidance if routing mix changes.

What we discussed (actionable):
1) Pricing structure we recommended on the call: tiered blanket rates with step-ups at 10M and 20M monthly committed volumes (see attached pricing workbook).
2) Blended-rate examples: we’ll show blended $/1M tokens for mixed routing (e.g., 70% v1, 30% v2) so procurement can budget.
3) Quick procurement path: draft addendum + DocuSign route for the additional committed capacity; procurement team to confirm legal/PO cadence.

Open items for you: please confirm the target budget range you want us to aim for (ballpark $/1M tokens) so we can optimize between blended discounts vs. model-level pricing. Also confirm whether the evaluation route should be capped (e.g., 30% of monthly tokens) or allowed to float.

Next steps (owners & timing):
- Marissa: send blended-rate examples + workbook (today).
- Jordan: confirm budget target $/1M and whether evaluation route is capped (by EOD Thu).
- Nikhil: prepare suggested SOW language for step-up tiers and blended-rate calc (by next Tue).

Attachments: redwood_renewal_pricing_v2.xlsx (workbook w/ tier math) — updated version coming in my follow-up.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme-health.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion — pricing & volume step-ups (post-call recap)

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Budget target: leadership is looking for a planning target of $800–1,000 per 1M tokens for baseline workloads. We understand Gen2 will be higher; can you show blended examples that land in that range for total bill?
2) Evaluation route: we’d like to start it at up to 30% of monthly tokens, ramping down or up depending on perf. We’d prefer an upper cap in the contract (30%) for budgeting.
3) Model mix: if ~30% goes to Gen2 (estimated 2x cost), what blended $/1M do you expect at 12M and 18M monthly volumes?

Procurement: looping you in to confirm doc/PO expectations.

—Jordan
VP Product, Acme Health
j.ellis@acme-health.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme-health.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-health.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion — pricing & volume step-ups (post-call recap)

Jordan / Samantha / procurement team —

Appreciate the clarity on the $/1M planning target. Attached is an updated workbook (redwood_renewal_pricing_v3.xlsx) and a short PDF summary with three scenarios. Quick highlights below (rounded):

Assumptions:
- v1 cost baseline: $900 / 1M tokens (current negotiated rate).
- v2 (Gen2) cost estimate: $1,900 / 1M tokens (higher perf model, better quality).
- Routing mix scenarios show blended $/1M at total committed volumes.

Scenario A — 12M/month (70% v1 / 30% v2):
- Weighted blended rate = (0.7 * $900) + (0.3 * $1,900) = $1,200 / 1M tokens
- With a 10% step-up discount on volumes >10M, effective blended = ~$1,080 / 1M
\Scenario B — 18M/month (70% v1 / 30% v2):
- Weighted blended = $1,200 / 1M (same mix)
- With tiered discounts (10% for 10–20M, 18% for >20M applied to v2-heavy usage), effective blended =~ $960–1,000 / 1M depending on exact split
\Scenario C — conservative cap on evaluation route (max 30%): ensures predictability; blended calc above uses that cap.

Notes on unit economics & recommendations:
- If Acme prioritizes staying near $800 / 1M overall, we recommend a higher committed volume (20M+) or a blended approach where lower-cost traffic is preferentially routed to v1 and evaluation trials are capped at 20% initially.
- We can also offer a temporary promotional credit on Gen2 route for the first 3 months of ramp to accelerate evaluation while protecting budget.

Attachments in this message: redwood_renewal_pricing_v3.xlsx (workbook with per-route model assumptions and line-item math), proposal_acme_health.pdf (draft addendum language + step-up tiers).

Next steps:
- Jordan: confirm if Acme is comfortable with the 30% cap (yes/no) and which scenario (12M ramp vs 18M ramp) is closer to your plan.
- Procurement: if green, we’ll send a draft addendum + DocuSign link for signature and a PO-ready invoice.

I’m free for a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow if you want to step through the workbook.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
